column3: Ch.11 commercial bankruptcies will sustain >40% YoY acceleration through Q2 2026 as tariff costs compound existing business stress
column7: Apr 17 update: Confidence REDUCED from 70% to 65%. March monthly Ch.11 -11% MoM vs prior year is a headwind. IEEPA refunds + lower Section 122 rate (vs IEEPA peak) may delay some business failures. Q1 average still +37% YoY; trajectory is to sustain but the monthly March data introduces doubt about Q2 sustaining >40%.
column9: Ch.11 was +37% in Q1 2026 (just at threshold). Tariffs active April 2026 will add cost pressure. Historical pattern: stress acceleration accelerates before plateauing. Invalidation: tariff relief, Fed rate cuts, major fiscal stimulus.

column3: NFIB Optimism Index will drop below 95 by June 2026 as tariff reality hits small business sentiment
column7: Apr 17 update: Confidence UPGRADED from 65% to 80%. March reading is 95.8 — only 0.8pt above the 95 trigger. 3-point single-month drop is the largest in this declining trend. April NFIB will capture oil price shock (peak late March/April), Jul 24 tariff cliff anxiety, and ongoing profit pressure. Very likely to breach 95 by June.
column9: Currently 95.8 (Mar 2026); 3rd consecutive monthly decline; 0.8pt above 95 threshold. April NFIB (~May 13) will be critical. Invalidation: tariff clarity (Section 301 replacement announced), energy price relief, strong consumer demand surge.

column3: Subchapter V small business bankruptcy elections will exceed +80% YoY by Q3 2026 (currently +67%)
column7: Apr 17 update: Confidence UPGRADED from 60% to 70%. February 2026 standalone was +91% YoY — already above the 80% Q3 target. Q1 avg of +67% means Jan/Mar were lower; Feb was a spike. Trajectory is clearly toward +80%+ sustained by Q3.
column9: Subch.V is the most direct small business stress measure. +91% YoY in Feb alone. Q1 avg +67%. IEEPA refunds may provide temporary relief but structural business stress persists. Invalidation: tariff rollback, significant improvement in business credit access, Section 122 replaced with lower rate.

column3: Restaurant sector will see 700+ QSR chain location closures (Wendy's + Pizza Hut + Papa John's combined) confirmed in H1 2026
column7: Apr 17 update: Confidence UPGRADED from 80% to 95%. Wendy's 300-350 + Pizza Hut 250 + Papa John's 200 = 750-800 alone. Bahama Breeze 14 completed Apr 15. Jack in Box 50-100 in progress. Original 700 threshold essentially confirmed from company announcements alone.
column9: NEAR-CONFIRMED at company level. Wendy's + Pizza Hut + Papa John's alone = 750-800. Adding Jack in Box, Noodles, Bahama Breeze = 944-1,049 FY total. Invalidation: companies reverse closure plans (very unlikely given company filings/earnings guidance).

column3: Total U.S. retail store closures will exceed 10,000 in 2026 (vs 7,900 base case Coresight projection)
column7: Apr 17 update: Confidence UPGRADED from 65% to 70%. 1,200+ closures publicly announced YTD; on trajectory toward high end of range. Section 122 10% replaces IEEPA rates but still represents cost pressure for retail importers; IEEPA refunds provide one-time cash. Net: slightly lower urgency than peak IEEPA but trajectory continues.
column9: Coresight projects 7,900; 1,200+ announced; Section 122 (10% vs prior IEEPA peak) still burdens retail importers. Consumer spending softening. Invalidation: tariff relief specifically for retail imports; consumer spending rebound; IEEPA refunds creating enough liquidity to delay closures.

column3: SBA 7(a) default rate will breach 5% (ORANGE threshold) by Q4 2026 driven by 2020-21 vintage loan maturities plus tariff-stressed 2022-23 vintage
column7: Apr 17 update: Confidence REDUCED from 55% to 50%. IEEPA tariff removal + IEEPA refunds ($166B, many to small businesses) may provide enough liquidity to push some defaults past year-end. Section 122 10% still pressures margins but less than IEEPA 125%+ [FLAGGED WRONG pre-Apr-17 — actual ~20%; correct at Jul-24 refresh]. Path from 3.4% to 5% still requires 160bps; now less certain timing.
column9: Currently ~3.4% (YELLOW). Competing forces: 2020-21 vintage maturity cycle (drives higher) vs IEEPA refund liquidity (pushes timeline out). Invalidation: IEEPA refunds absorbed before EOY + tariff relief + SBA restructuring program.

column3: 2026 Fed SBCS annual report (published 2027, data from 2026 survey) will show revenue and employment expectations below 2020 COVID levels
column7: Apr 17 update: Confidence UPGRADED from 65% to 70%. NFIB March profit trend at -25% (worst since COVID) is a strong leading indicator that SBCS 2026 survey respondents will report deterioration below 2020 levels. The SBCS survey is annual and will capture the full tariff uncertainty period.
column9: 2025 SBCS at 2020 lows (33 revenue, 23 employment). NFIB March profit trend -25% (worst since COVID) strongly suggests 2026 SBCS will show below-2020 readings. Invalidation: meaningful economic recovery in H2 2026 + tariff resolution before SBCS survey period.

column3: Owner compensation cuts will be documented above 40% in next major small business owner survey (Truist 2025 report or BofA H2 2026)
column9: No new survey data available Apr 17. Prior: Truist 50% (lifetime), BofA 32% (12-month). NFIB March profit trend -25% is consistent with accelerating owner comp cuts. Invalidation: significant revenue recovery for small businesses before surveys conducted.
